Chapter 9: Maintaining Simplicity in a Complex World
Let’s face it—keeping life simple isn’t something you check off your to-do list and forget about. It’s a journey. The world keeps throwing new temptations, pressures, and, well, all sorts of complications your way. So how do you stick to that essential path when everything around you keeps changing?
Here are a few ongoing practices that really help anchor simplicity in your life.
First, make time for a regular review. Whether it’s every week or once a month, pause to look at your commitments, your habits, and even your stuff. Ask yourself, “What still feels essential? What could I let go of?”
Next, use natural transitions—like the start of a new year or a new season—as a chance for a reset. These moments are perfect for reassessing your goals and priorities.
Mindful consumption is key, too. Before you bring something new into your life, stop for a moment and ask, “Does this really add value?”
And maybe most importantly, embrace imperfection. Simplicity isn’t a destination you finally arrive at. There will always be areas of messiness or a little extra here and there. That’s totally okay.
Think about it like keeping a home tidy—not by doing one big clean-up, but by building little habits. You put things away each day, and regularly let go of what you no longer need. Simplicity in life works the same way—with small, steady actions.
Here’s a real-world example. Imagine a family that sits down every month to review their schedule. They look at which activities still bring them joy or fit their values, and let go of the ones that don’t. This ongoing process keeps their lives focused on what matters most.
So what’s a simple checklist to help you out?
Schedule regular decluttering sessions—both for your physical spaces and your digital world.
Revisit your “most important tasks” list. Update it as your goals or circumstances change.
And don’t forget to celebrate your progress. Take a moment to notice and appreciate all the ways your life feels easier and lighter.
When you make simplicity a living, breathing practice, you’ll find you can adapt to whatever comes your way—while staying grounded in what truly matters to you.
